subject: marine-science
intro: Marine science follows the ocean from physics to fisheries, and it leads to work reading the sea — measuring currents, assessing stocks, guarding ecosystems and teaching how the ocean works.

roles.title: Geoscientists, Except Hydrologists and Geographers
roles.what: Study the composition, structure and physical aspects of the Earth, including its oceans — using geological, physics and mathematics knowledge in exploration, environmental problems and the study of ocean and atmospheric forces.
roles.where: Ocean basins and plate tectonics from unit 1 and the physical chemistry of seawater — salinity, density, stratification, light and sound — are the oceanographic fundamentals the role applies daily.

roles.title: Hydrologists
roles.what: Research the distribution, circulation and physical properties of underground and surface waters, following precipitation through soil, rivers and aquifers on its return to the ocean and atmosphere.
roles.where: Tides and sea level from unit 1, and the chemistry and circulation of seawater in units 2 and 3, ground the coastal and estuarine hydrology — where rivers meet the sea — that this work involves.

roles.title: Zoologists and Wildlife Biologists
roles.what: Study the origins, behaviour, diseases, genetics and life processes of animals and wildlife, analysing biological data to judge how uses of land and water habitats affect them — in this case, marine animals.
roles.where: Marine ecosystems from shore to trench, plankton and primary production, and the physiology unit's osmoregulation, gas exchange and buoyancy give the organism-level grounding for studying sea life.

roles.title: Atmospheric, Earth, Marine, and Space Sciences Teachers, Postsecondary
roles.what: Teach courses in the physical sciences other than chemistry and physics — oceanography among them — combining lectures and laboratories with research on the systems they teach.
roles.where: This course's syllabus, from seawater chemistry through fisheries to ocean and climate, is a ready-made university teaching sequence, with El Niño and the carbon pump as marquee lectures.
